messages.subject: Initializing 'data' argument in nimbleModel function
parts:
I'd originally assumed that setting the 'data' argument in the nimbleModel function served as like an initialization or a default value as with typical functions. But when I run the model, the results (samples) differ depending on what was fed into 'data' initially, even if I try and reassign the value later (third-to-last and second-to-last lines). Can anyone explain to me why this is?

library(nimble)

#==========================================================

# Simulate some data

#==========================================================

lon <- lat <- seq(from=0,to=10,length=25)

grid <- expand.grid(lon = lon,lat = lat)

trueMean <- 5

C_chol <- chol(exp(-as.matrix(dist(grid))/2))

N <- nrow(grid)

K <- 20


# Generate observations

set.seed(0)

obs <- as.numeric(rep(trueMean,N) + t(C_chol) %*% rnorm(N))


# Generate K data sets

models <- matrix(NA, N, K)

set.seed(2)

for(r in 1:K) {

  models[,r] <- as.numeric(rep(trueMean,N) + t(C_chol) %*% rnorm(N))

}


#==========================================================

# Set up Bayesian models and MCMC with nimble

#==========================================================

Rcode <- nimbleCode({

  # likelihood ==============

  for(i in 1:N) Y[i] ~ dnorm( mean = X[i], sd = sigma )

  # process =================

  X[1:N] <- Xmat[1:N,1:K] %*% norm_weights[1:K]

  norm_weights[1:K] <- weights[1:K] / sum(weights[1:K])

  # prior distributions =====

  for(k in 1:K) weights[k] ~ dunif(0,1)

  sigma ~ dunif(0,10000)

})


# Set up model

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(

  code = Rcode,

  constants = list(N = N, K = K),

  inits = list( weights = rep(1/K,K) ),

  data = list( Y = rnorm(N), Xmat = matrix(rnorm(N*K)*2, nrow = N) )    #  I get different answers depending on whether this line or the next one is commented out.

#  data = list( Y = obs, Xmat = models )

)

comp <- compileNimble(Rmodel)

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)

conf$printSamplers()

conf$addMonitors("norm_weights")

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)

Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)


#==========================================================

# Run MCMC

#==========================================================

# Attach actual data

comp$Y <- obs

comp$Xmat <- models

samples <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, niter = 1e5)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Initializing 'data' argument in nimbleModel function
parts:
Hi Alex,

Thanks for the question and the reproducible example.

I think your question is about why you are not getting exactly identical samples (but samples in either case should be statistically valid and sampling the same posterior).

It looks like the reason this is happening is that you do a set.seed at the top, but then of the two variants you have, one of them draws some random numbers and the other doesn't.  This means the random number generator will be in a different state when runMCMC starts, and that means it will go through a different sequence of random draws involved in the MCMC sampling.  If you do another set.seed before runMCMC, you should see identical samples.  I've confirmed that on my machine.

At first I thought another reason is that you have not initialized sigma.  There is a message from nimbleModel that the model is not fully initialized.  Then Rmodel$initializeInfo() says it is sigma that is not initialized.  That means a value will be drawn from the prior (potentially a very bad value since the prior is uninformative).  But as long as the RNG is in the same state in both of your variants, the same prior value for sigma should be drawn.  So it would be a good idea to initialize sigma, but that should not be a reason to see different MCMC outcomes as I at first suspected.

HTH!  Take care.

Perry
